blocks.h1: Approvals and purchase orders: no invoice goes out without its PO.
blocks.lead: Relvo prepares the draft invoice, obtains the purchase order or approval your customer requires, and issues only when everything matches.
blocks.intro: When you sell to businesses, an invoice without its purchase order or service entry sheet gets rejected. The first days of the month go into requesting documents, checking them against contracts and reissuing invoices. With Relvo, every invoice goes out with its supporting documents linked and approved.

blocks.h2: From requesting a PO by email to an approved invoice.
before: Invoices rejected because a purchase order is missing.
Back-and-forth emails to obtain the PO or service entry sheet.
Someone manually checks that the PO matches the contract.
after: Every invoice goes out with its PO linked.
An agent follows up by email until the document arrives.
If the PO does not match, Relvo sends it to review before issuing.

blocks.h2: Your customer's process, without writing every email.

items.title: Configurable routing
items.text: Each contract defines who approves: your team, the customer or both, and in which order.

items.title: Draft before issuance
items.text: A draft awaiting approval prevents issuing anything that has not been confirmed.

items.title: PO and service entry sheet matching
items.text: Relvo checks that the customer's document matches the invoice; if it does not, it notifies the account owner.

items.title: Slack and dedicated email
items.text: The agent requests, reminds and responds where your team already works.

items.title: Automatic issuance
items.text: Once approval is complete, the invoice and its tax document are issued without manual intervention.

blocks.h2Soft: The same engine, from end to end.

blocks.h2: Frequently asked questions about approvals and purchase orders.

items.q: What is a service entry sheet (HES)?
items.a: A service entry sheet, known as HES in Chile, is a document many customers require alongside the purchase order to accept an invoice. Relvo links it to the invoice just like the PO.
Yes. An agent reads the PO, extracts details such as its number, amount and validity period, and links it to the corresponding draft invoice.

items.q: What happens if the PO does not match the contract?
items.a: Relvo does not issue the invoice. It stays in a review inbox, where your team decides whether to request a new PO or approve it anyway.
Yes. You can configure approval flows for your team and the customer before issuing.

items.q: Does it work with customers who do not require POs?
items.a: Yes. If a customer does not require a purchase order or approval, their invoice goes out directly when the period ends.
Each contract defines this: your team, the customer or both, and in which order.

items.q: When does a case escalate to my team?
items.a: When the customer disputes the amount or the purchase order does not cover the invoice. The rest of the process runs automatically.
